ai.title: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
ai.brief: Today’s LLMs are engineered to disobey dangerous requests. But AI refusal is far from foolproof—and could become an instrument of repression. Ever since people first seriously contemplated giving machines an intelligence modeled on our own, there has never been any question that they would, like us, be able to say no. The sci-fi canon is full of stories of robotic disobedience. Most of these capers are, of course, cautionary. But recently, the idea that AI shouldn’t do everything you ask has become something like a commandment. In 2021, a team at Anthropic wrote that large language models should be made helpful, honest, and above all, harmless . g. ” Who can argue with that?

sec.title: Co-creator of Empire Market dark web marketplace given 40-year sentence
sec.brief: The co-creator of a dark web cybercriminal forum called Empire Market was sentenced this week to 40 years in federal prison for his role in helping people sell drugs, hacking tools and stolen information. Raheim Hamilton, 30, pleaded guilty earlier this year to a drug conspiracy charge and agreed to forfeit more than $100 million worth of Bitcoin and several properties in Virginia. S. District Judge Steven Seeger issued the 40-year sentence and fined him $5 million. The Virginia native partnered with Thomas Pavey in owning and operating Empire Market from 2018 to 2020. The platform quickly became popular among drug dealers and cybercriminals — allowing them to sell narcotics, stolen account credentials, stolen documents, fake currency and hacking tools. More than 4 million transactions were conducted on the site for a total volume of $430 million.
